To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

in a cross‐sectional study, even among non‐insulin‐dependent diabetics with generally low high‐density lipoprotein (HDL) and HDL2 cholesterols, the presence of coronary heart disease is associated with a depression of HDL2 cholestrol levels.
the presence of CHd is associated with a lower concentration of HDL and of HDL2 cholesterol in NIDDs, even among those with generally low HDl and HDL2 values.

in a cross‐sectional study, even among noninsulin‐dependent diabetics (with generally low high‐density lipoprotein [HDL] and HDL2‐cholesterol concentrations), the presence of coronary heart disease is associated with a still lower HDL and HDl2 cholesterol levels.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of lipids in the etiology of CHD.
the association of low HDL and high LDL cholesterol with CHD in noninsulin-dependent diabetes (NIDD).
the role of lipids and lipoprotein in the development of coronary heart disease.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
low HDL cholesterol is a risk factor for CHD in NIDDM.
low HDL cholesterol is associated with an increased risk of coronary heart disease in NIDDs, and that this association is independent of other coronary risk factors.
HDL2 is a risk factor for CHD in NIDDs, and that the presence of CHL is associated with further reduction in HDL2 levels.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
HDL and HDLC are associated with CHD in noninsulin-dependent diabetes mellitus.
the HDL and HDLC2 cholesterol concentrations are inversely associated with the presence of coronary heart disease in NIDDs.
the association of low HDL and CHD is not a consequence of the disease but a risk factor for the disease.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the association between low HDL cholesterol and CHD is not restricted to the general population, but also holds for NIDDs.
HDL is not a good predictor of cardiovascular disease in patients with diabetes.
the association between HDL cholesterol and CHD is stronger in men than in women.
